- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early days of the 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.10), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price action shows resilience or reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ in 3-5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1-2% for the next 3-5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 1-3% for next 5-7 days; if below, increase by 1-2% if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- Horizon-specific: 1st day of 30d forecast often overestimates; reduce by 0.5–1.5% for day 1–3; 2nd–5th days show lagged bias; adjust based on sentiment momentum (e.g., if sentiment rising, reduce forecast slightly; if falling, increase).
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or flat sentiment, model tends to overfit recent noise; apply smoothing: average last 5–7 days’ true values before forecasting.
